slides.say: x is a two-digit number. x is equal to the cube of its units digit, plus four times the sum of its digits. What is the tens digit of x?
A digit puzzle in words, with no columns. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the algebraic form, and then plugging in the answers.
[short pause] Let's start with the algebraic form. The tens digit is T and the units digit is U, so x is ten T plus U. And the condition, x equals U cubed, plus four times T plus U.
at: x is ten T plus U

slides.say: Open the bracket, four T plus four U. Take four T and one U away from both sides. Six T equals U cubed plus three U.

Six T is at most six times nine, fifty-four, so U is small. U one gives one plus three, four. U two, eight plus six, fourteen. U three, twenty-seven plus nine, thirty-six. U four, sixty-four plus twelve, seventy-six, too big. Only thirty-six is six times a digit.
Six T is thirty-six, so T is six. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way, plugging in the answers. What's different? We start from each tens digit they offer. Seven? Then x is seventy plus U, and the condition is U cubed, plus twenty-eight, plus four U. Take twenty-eight and U away, U cubed plus three U is forty-two. U three gives thirty-six, U four gives seventy-six. No digit works. Out.
The same way, five needs thirty, and four needs twenty-four. No digit gives those. Out.

Six needs thirty-six, and U three gives exactly that. So x is sixty-three. Three cubed is twenty-seven, and four times nine is thirty-six. Twenty-seven plus thirty-six is sixty-three. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
